question: A hospital is planning to migrate its patient records system from on-premises servers to a hybrid cloud solution. Analyse the hardware, software, networking, security, and backup considerations involved in this migration. Discuss the benefits and risks of this approach in relation to GDPR compliance, data security threats, and business continuity.
markingGuidance: Award marks for: hardware considerations in hybrid setup (1 mark), software architecture/licensing (1 mark), networking requirements (WAN/VPN) (1 mark), security measures (encryption, access control) (1 mark), backup/disaster recovery (1 mark), GDPR compliance discussion (1 mark), risk analysis (data residency, third-party access) (1 mark), business continuity benefits (1 mark). Expect discussion of scalability, cost, accessibility, and regulatory requirements.

question: A retail chain operates 50 stores across the country. Each store has its own LAN connected via WAN to a central data centre. Discuss the network architecture, hardware components at each location, and security measures needed to protect customer payment data. Analyse the backup strategy required to prevent loss of transaction records and ensure GDPR compliance for customer information stored across this distributed system.
markingGuidance: Award marks for: LAN/WAN architecture explanation (1 mark), hardware components identified (1 mark), security measures for payment data (1 mark), PCI DSS/compliance mention (1 mark), backup strategy design (1 mark), encryption/data protection (1 mark), GDPR considerations (1 mark), disaster recovery plan (1 mark). Expect discussion of redundancy, monitoring, and incident response.

question: A bank has experienced a data breach affecting customer financial information. Analyse the possible security threats that led to the breach, the steps the organisation must take under GDPR, and a comprehensive backup and recovery strategy to prevent future incidents. Discuss how cloud services and advanced security technologies could strengthen the bank's defences.
markingGuidance: Award marks for: identification of breach vectors (malware, phishing, weak security) (1 mark), GDPR notification and investigation requirements (1 mark), affected individual notification (1 mark), backup recovery procedures (1 mark), security hardening measures (1 mark), cloud security benefits (1 mark), encryption and access controls (1 mark), incident response planning (1 mark). Expect discussion of regulatory penalties, trust restoration, and lessons learned.

question: A large school with 1000 students needs to implement a complete IT infrastructure for online learning, including LANs in different buildings, cloud-based applications, and secure storage of student records. Explain the hardware, networking, and cloud service requirements. Analyse the security threats unique to educational environments and propose appropriate mitigation strategies. Discuss GDPR considerations for student and staff data protection.
markingGuidance: Award marks for: hardware specifications for multi-building LAN (1 mark), networking infrastructure (Wi-Fi, switches, routers) (1 mark), cloud service selection (SaaS for applications) (1 mark), security threats in schools (inappropriate content, student data, unauthorised access) (1 mark), mitigation strategies (filters, access controls, monitoring) (1 mark), GDPR student data handling (1 mark), staff privacy considerations (1 mark), backup and disaster recovery for educational records (1 mark).

question: Analyse the complete lifecycle of data protection in a distributed enterprise using multiple software systems, LANs, WANs, and cloud services. From data collection through deletion, discuss security threats at each stage, appropriate safeguards, backup strategies, GDPR compliance measures, and disaster recovery planning. Use a real-world scenario (retail, hospital, school, or bank) to illustrate your answer, and evaluate how hybrid cloud architecture could improve the organization's resilience and regulatory compliance.
markingGuidance: Award marks for: data collection phase security (consent, GDPR) (1 mark), storage security (encryption, access controls) (1 mark), transmission security (VPN, TLS) (1 mark), processing security (software security, authentication) (1 mark), backup and recovery procedures (1 mark), threat analysis across phases (1 mark), deletion/data retention compliance (1 mark), comprehensive GDPR compliance and hybrid cloud benefits (1 mark). Expect integrated discussion of all topic areas with critical analysis.
